question.problem:
Consider the function $f,$ defined as 

$$
f({x}_{1},{x}_{2})={x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}.
$$

What is the shape of the total derivative of $f$ with respect to $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
The total derivative of a scalar-valued function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ with respect to a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ is the row vector

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{1\times n}.
$$

In our case, the function 

- acts on a vector $x\in {R}^{2},$ and

- outputs a scalar $f({x}_{1},{x}_{2})\in R.$

Therefore, the total derivative will be a row vector of shape $1\times 2.$
